verdict: AppLovin's advertising platform grew revenue 73% from a year ago to $999M and turned it into $596M of profit from continuing operations — a 63% operating margin — while the apps business it later sold chipped in a small $3M profit of its own.

segments.name: Advertising platform
segments.note: Ads placed through AppLovin's AXON platform — advertisers pay to reach users inside other companies' apps, and AXON's AI decides which ads to show. AppLovin sold its own apps business in June 2025; its results sit in discontinued operations, below.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building and improving the AXON ad platform — the restated figure excludes the apps business.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to advertisers and app publishers.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $94M on AppLovin's debt, including a loss on settling debt early during a late-2024 refinancing, partly offset by $0.3M of other income — plus a $3M profit from the apps business AppLovin sold in June 2025, which accounting rules report as discontinued operations.
follow100Note: The tax line added money back this quarter — a $61M benefit — and the 'other expense' step nets $94M of interest and debt-settlement costs against a $3M profit from the sold apps business. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The platform's breakout year
takeaways.text: Advertising revenue rose 73% from a year ago to $999M in the quarter — and $3.22B for the full year, up 75%. AXON, AppLovin's AI ad engine, kept finding better matches between advertisers and the users inside other companies' apps.

takeaways.title: Margins most companies can't match
takeaways.text: The continuing platform turned $999M of revenue into $628M of operating income. Its total costs were just $371M — they barely grow with sales, so most of each new revenue dollar drops through to profit.

takeaways.title: A tax benefit, not a tax bill
takeaways.text: The continuing business recorded a $61M income-tax benefit this quarter, adding directly to profit. Together with a small $3M profit from the apps business being sold, reported net income reached $599M.

oneTimers: A $61M income-tax benefit in continuing operations — the tax line added to profit instead of subtracting from it.
Interest expense of $94M includes a loss on settling debt early, as AppLovin refinanced its borrowings in late 2024.
footerNote: AppLovin reports as a single segment. The flow shows the continuing advertising-platform business, as restated in AppLovin's Q4 2025 release after the apps business was sold in June 2025; the apps business's $3M profit is folded into the 'other' step so the bottom line matches the reported net income of $599M. The continuing platform earned $596M. When Q4 was first reported in February 2025, the apps business was still included and total revenue was $1,373M.
